- Model tends to overestimate prices in early periods of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, often missing upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Overreacts to recent volatility, producing exaggerated downward corrections after spikes.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10 days, then gradually adjusts downward — may need to apply a smoothing or decay factor.
- Fails to capture mean reversion in the middle of the forecast, often holding too high a value when prices are trending down.
- Sensitive to recent low values — may underestimate recovery if recent prices are too low.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of price rebounds after corrections — especially in the 15–25 day window.
- Overestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to overly conservative or pessimistic forecasts.
- Lags in capturing short-term reversals — often misses sudden price drops or spikes in the last 3–5 days.
- Underestimates the impact of policy or market events — may not adjust forecasts quickly enough to reflect new information.
